title: Unique gluing of derived maps locally in degree zero
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\tau$ be its small etale or small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, regarded as a constant sheaf. Work in $D(T_\tau,A)$, the ordinary derived category of sheaves of $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed Zariski open cover of $T$, with exact derived restrictions denoted by $|_{U_i}$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Let $M,N\in D(T_\tau,A)$, and assume
$$\mathcal H^a(M|_{U_i})=\mathcal H^a(N|_{U_i})=0\quad\text{for every }i\in I\text{ and }a\ne0.$$
Then $\mathcal H^a(M)=\mathcal H^a(N)=0$ for $a\ne0$, and the good-truncation maps [def-kun-truncations] induce canonical isomorphisms $M\cong\mathcal H^0(M)[0]$ and $N\cong\mathcal H^0(N)[0]$, natural in these objects and commuting with restriction. Restriction induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T_\tau,A)}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\left\{(a_i)\in\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D((U_i)_\tau,A)}(M|_{U_i},N|_{U_i}):a_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=a_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\text{ for all }i,j\right\}.$$
Under the canonical degree-zero identifications this is exactly unique gluing of the $A$-module sheaf maps $\mathcal H^0(M)|_{U_i}\to\mathcal H^0(N)|_{U_i}$. In particular equality of two such global derived maps can be checked on this cover. The assertion includes the empty scheme and its empty open cover; it asserts no gluing property for arbitrary derived complexes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-open-cover-cohomology-detection] to the given cover and to $K=M,N$. Its degreewise vanishing criterion gives $\mathcal H^a(M)=\mathcal H^a(N)=0$ for $a\ne0$. Its ringed-site identifications supply the same constant coefficients, exact restrictions and overlap sites as in the statement, and make the Zariski cover and all its pullbacks site coverings. This includes the empty cover.

source.place: Tag 04IX, definition-localize-ringed-site, part (4); Sites Tag 00VR, definition-sheaf. Agent-formulated combination with the two small-site localization equivalences; source details and the full inherited argument are retained in report.md.

proof.text: The module-sheaf categories are abelian [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-pur-good-truncation-exact-normalization] in the abelian module-sheaf category on $T_\tau$, and on each open and intersection. It gives the specified good-truncation isomorphisms $\epsilon_M,\epsilon_N$, natural in all derived maps. Apply its exact-functor formula with the open restrictions of Step 1: these isomorphisms commute with restriction and with iterated restriction. Put $F=\mathcal H^0(M)$ and $G=\mathcal H^0(N)$. The same lemma gives the Hom bijection $a\mapsto b=\mathcal H^0(a)$, characterized by $b[0]=\epsilon_Na\epsilon_M^{-1}$, and its restriction square. Thus compatible local derived maps correspond exactly to compatible local module-sheaf maps.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical cochain truncation at zero; Derived Categories Tag 06XS, lemma-negative-exts (2). Agent-formulated normalization and exact-functor compatibility, with inherited derivation and further localization references in report.md.

proof.text: For compatible $(a_i)$ let $b_i$ be their sheaf maps from Step 2. The covering and fiber products supplied in Step 1 allow [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] to give a unique global $b:F\to G$. Set $a=\epsilon_N^{-1}b[0]\epsilon_M$. The restriction square gives $a|_{U_i}=a_i$. Conversely two global derived maps with equal restrictions give sheaf maps with equal restrictions; uniqueness of $b$ and the Hom bijection make them equal. This proves the claimed bijection, its identification with sheaf-map gluing, and the equality test. On the empty scheme Step 1 makes all module sheaves zero, Step 2 identifies $M,N$ with zero objects, and the empty-cover gluing assertion still gives the unique map.
